correctness.rationale: In each chain factor, annihilator classes are exactly valuation levels, so product classes are valuation vectors and adjacency is coordinatewise threshold addition. For r>=2 the vertex w_i with valuation one in coordinate i and zero elsewhere has the unique neighbour d_i with all other coordinates maximal and coordinate i one below maximal; hence every total dominating set contains all d_i. The d_i form a clique and every nonunit/nonzero valuation vector has a positive coordinate, so that clique totally dominates. Even r gives a perfect matching inside the core; odd r requires one extra vertex, which can always be matched to a core vertex corresponding to a positive coordinate. Fresh exhaustive checks on representative local, two-factor and three-factor valuation graphs reproduced the claimed total and paired minima and counts.

final_claim: For the annihilator-compressed zero-divisor graph of a finite commutative principal ideal ring, every nonlocal product with r local chain-ring factors has a unique forced r-vertex minimum total-dominating core, paired domination equals r for even r and r+1 for odd r with the exact stated minimum-set classification and count, while the local cases have the stated isolated or two-vertex behavior.
